Package hadur2.core.memory

Class ProfileLibrary

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.memory.ProfileLibrary
public final class ProfileLibrary extends Object
Loads and saves opponent profiles in a ProfileStore. It owns everything that makes persistence safe, so the store adapters stay thin:
  • MEM-4: a profile that is missing reads as a stranger; one that is damaged, or a store that throws, also reads as a stranger and counts a load failure.
  • RES-3: a save writes the new bytes to <file>.tmp first, then over the profile, then deletes the temporary copy. A robot killed during the first write leaves the old profile intact; one killed during the second leaves a complete temporary copy, which the next load uses. (Robocode's sandbox forbids renaming files, so the copy stands in for the usual rename.) Checksums tell a complete copy from a torn one.
  • MEM-5: before writing, if the store would pass EVICT_AT of its quota, the seeds of the least recently fought other profiles are dropped until it would not. If the write still would not fit, this profile's own seeds go; if even the stats alone do not fit, the write is skipped and counted.
  • A battle counter in CLOCK stamps each profile with when it was last fought, which is what "least recently fought" means.

Nothing here throws: every failure becomes a counter and a note. The core copies the counters into each round's R record (RES-5) and writes the note as a MEM line.

One library lives for the whole battle, created by HadurCore only for a duel with a store. The robot calls prepare() before the first tick, the core calls load(java.lang.String) at the first scan (MEM-1), and save(hadur2.core.memory.OpponentProfile) at the end of each round Hadur survives and at the battle's end (MEM-3).

Store files: <stem>.hp for each profile (the stem from LineageKey.fileStem(java.lang.String)), <stem>.hp.tmp for the temporary copy while a save is in progress, and CLOCK.

    • ProfileLibrary

      public ProfileLibrary(ProfileStore store, int writeVersion)
      MEM-7: a library that writes every profile — regular saves, eviction rewrites and stats-only checkpoints alike — at writeVersion instead of the codec's current one, so a client still on a previous release can go on reading what this one writes. ProfileCodec.decode(byte[]) reads any version back to ProfileCodec.OLDEST_VERSION, whatever this library writes, so nothing here needs to change to read older files.
      Parameters:
      store - where the profiles live; the robot's data directory or an in-memory map
      writeVersion - the format version to write, ProfileCodec.OLDEST_VERSION to ProfileCodec.VERSION

    • save

      public ProfileLibrary.Saved save(OpponentProfile profile)
      MEM-3: persists profile atomically within the quota. Never throws.

      The space check assumes the worst moment of a save: the temporary copy and the profile both on disk, plus the clock. If that would pass EVICT_AT of the quota, other profiles' seeds go first (MEM-5); if it would still pass the whole quota, this profile's own seeds go; if even that does not fit, nothing is written. MEM-6: that last case cannot happen while any other profile still has seeds, because evictSeeds(java.lang.String, long) never stops short of freeing what EVICT_AT's threshold needs unless it has already taken every seed there was to take (its target is always at or under the hard quota checked here) — so a write is only ever skipped once nothing more can be evicted from anyone.

      Parameters:
      profile - the profile to save
      Returns:
      what was done

    • saveStatsOnly

      public ProfileLibrary.Saved saveStatsOnly(OpponentProfile profile)
      TIME-4: writes profile's statistics without re-writing its seeds from scratch. Round-end checkpoints use this so the frequent write costs only what the stats need: it never serialises the caller's own (possibly large) seed lists, and never touches them in memory either. Whatever seeds are already safely on disk for this profile are carried over unchanged, so a checkpoint before the tenth never erases what an earlier save already committed (MEM-3) — it only leaves them stale until the next full save (battle end, or every tenth checkpoint, see HadurCore#checkpoint), never gone.
      Parameters:
      profile - the profile to save
      Returns:
      what was done
